Rashi on Pesachim 37a:10:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי לא נחתומין אמרו - לאסור, שרגילין ובקיאין בדבר ויש להן דפוסין:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:10:1.english: Some say [they] did not say [this of] bakers - to prohibit [it], for they are accustomed to and expert in the matter, and they have molds.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:10:2.hebrew: עושין סריקין - מצויירין, כמין רקיקין, ובלבד שיהו דקין וקלושין, דאין ממהרין להחמיץ, אבל לא מציירין את העבים כגלוסקאות, דמתוך עוביין מחמיצין בשהייה מועטת:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:10:2.english: One may make serikin - [That is,] patterned [matzot], shaped like thin wafers, provided that they are thin and fine, since they do not leaven quickly; however, one may not pattern the thick ones like thick loaves [geluskaot], because due to their thickness they leaven in a brief delay.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:1.english: The sponge-cakes [hasufganin] - [They are] made like a sponge.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:2.hebrew: והדובשנין - מטוגנין בדבש, וכולן מין לחם: המסרת - תרגום של מחבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:2.english: And the honey cakes - [They are] fried in honey, and all of them are a type of bread. Hamasret - [This is] the Aramaic translation of machavat [a frying pan].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:3.hebrew: והאיסקריטין - עשויין כצפיחית דמתרגמינן איסקריטון (שמות טז), שלשין עיסתן רכה מאד:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:3.english: And the iskaritin - [They are] made like tzapichit [wafers], which we translate [in the Targum as] iskariton (Exodus 16), whose dough they knead very soft.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:4.english: Hamasret - [This is the Aramaic] translation of maḥavat [a frying pan].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:5.hebrew: והמדומע - חולין שנפלה תרומה לתוכן, פטור, דתרימו תרומה כתיב, ולא שכבר היה תרומה:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:5.english: And a mixture - Non-sacred [grain] into which teruma fell [is] exempt, for it is written, "you shall set aside teruma," and not [from something] that was already teruma.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:6.hebrew: ופטורין מן החלה - דכתיב (במדבר ט״ו:י״ט) "באכלכם מלחם הארץ", והני לאו לחם נינהו, ולקמיה מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:6.english: And they are exempt from challah - For it is written (Numbers 15:19): "When you eat of the bread of the land," and these are not [considered] bread; and later [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:11:7.english: Boiled [bread] of homeowners - It is not made in the [standard] manner of bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:12:1.hebrew: ריש לקיש אכולהו קאי, ולא לאפלוגי אד<abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> יהושע בן לוי אתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:12:1.english: Reish Lakish refers to all of them, and he did not come to disagree with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:12:2.hebrew: מעשה אילפס הן - לפיכך לאו לחם הוא, דקא סבר אין לחם אלא האפוי בתנור, כדכתיב "לחמכם בתנור אחד" (ויקרא כ״ו:כ״ו):
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:12:2.english: They are made in a stewpot [ilpas] - Therefore it is not [considered] bread, for he holds [that] nothing is [considered] bread except what is baked in an oven, as it is written: "your bread in one oven" (Leviticus 26:26).

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:12:3.english: And these - For this reason they are exempt [from challah], because he made them in the sun and not over a fire.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:13:1.hebrew: שהרתיח - האילפס, ואחר כך הדביק בה הלחם, דהוה ליה כעין מעשה תנור. הלכך, חייבין:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:13:1.english: That he heated - the pot, and afterward pasted the bread [dough] to it, so that it is like an oven's [baking] process. Therefore, they are obligated [in challah].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:16:1.hebrew: הינא - אינה אפויה כל צורכה, לשון "אל תאכלו ממנו נא" (שמות י״ב:ט׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:16:1.english: Hina - It is not baked all that it needs [to be]; [similar to the] expression, "Do not eat of it raw [na]" (Exodus 12:9).

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:16:2.hebrew: העשויה באילפס - ואע"ג דלחם בעינן, כדכתיב "לחם עוני" (דברים טז):
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:16:2.english: [Matza] made in a pot - Even though we require bread, as it is written: "bread of affliction" (Deuteronomy 16[:3])[, nonetheless one fulfills the obligation with it].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:17:1.hebrew: מאי מצה הינא - כלומר, כמה תאפה ויהא יוצא בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:17:1.english: What is half-baked matza - That is to say, how much must it be baked so that one fulfills [his obligation] with it?

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:17:2.english: That one breaks it - That one breaks it; [related to the] expression perusah [a broken piece].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:17:3.hebrew: וכן לענין לחמי תודה - אם שחט הזבח עליהן מאחר שנאפת כענין הזה, קידש הלחם והתודה כשירה, דהואיל וקרמו פניה, דתנן במנחות כי האי גוונא בעינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:17:3.english: And likewise with respect to the loaves of the thanks-offering - If one slaughtered the sacrifice over them after it was baked in this manner, the bread is sanctified and the thanks-offering is valid; for since its surface has formed a crust — as we learned in [Tractate] Menachot, we require such [a degree of baking].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:1:1.hebrew: וכמה פת עבה טפח - ואפי' הכי שרו בית הלל, אבל טפי מטפח לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:1:1.english: And how much [is] thick bread? A handbreadth - And even so, Beit Hillel permit [it], but more than a handbreadth, [they do] not.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:1:2.hebrew: שכן מצינו בלחם הפנים - שהוא אסור לבא חמץ, כדאמרינן במנחות (דף כז.): "כל המנחה אשר תקריבו וגו'", לרבות לחם הפנים לחימוץ, לאזהרה שלא יחמיצו; ואפילו הכי עובי דפנותיו טפח, דהיינו לחם שהיו לו פנים, ואין פנים פחותין מטפח:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:1:2.english: As we found with the shewbread - For it is forbidden to be brought [as] leavened [bread], as we say in Menachot (27a): "Every meal-offering which you shall bring, etc." — [this comes] to include the shewbread regarding leavening, as a warning not to leaven [it]; and even so, the thickness of its walls was a handbreadth, for that is bread that had faces, and faces are not less than a handbreadth.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:2:1.english: If they said - and permitted a thickness of a handbreadth.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:2:2.hebrew: לזריזין - כהנים שבקיאין בשימורו שלא יחמיץ, יתירו לכל אדם שאינן זריזין:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:2:2.english: To the diligent - priests who are expert in guarding it so that it does not become leavened — would they permit [it] to anyone who is not diligent?

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:2:3.hebrew: בפת עמילה - שאינה ממהרת להחמיץ, שעמילתה מעכבתה. עמילה — ברייר"א, כדתנן (מנחות דף עו.) כל המנחות טעונין שלש מאות שיפה וחמש מאות בעיטה:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:2:3.english: With well-kneaded bread - Which does not hasten to become leavened, for its [thorough] kneading holds it back [from leavening]. Amilah [means] broyer [in Old French, i.e., kneading], as we learned in a Mishnah (Menachot 76a): All meal-offerings require three hundred rubbings and five hundred poundings.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:3:1.hebrew: בעצים יבשים - שהיו מביאים אותן מימות החמה, כדאמרינן בתענית (דף לא.): מחמשה עשר באב ואילך, תשש כחה של חמה ולא היו כורתין עצים למערכה:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:3:1.english: With dry wood - For they would bring them from the summer days, as we say in Taanit (31a): From the fifteenth of Av and onward, the strength of the sun weakens and they would not cut wood for the [altar] pyre.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:3:2.hebrew: בתנור חם - בכל יום תמיד היו מסיקין תנור של מקדש לאפיית מנחות ולחמי תודה, ושל מתכת היה, כדאמר בזבחים בפ' דם חטאת (זבחים דף צה:):
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:3:2.english: With a hot oven - Every day, constantly, they would heat the Temple oven for baking meal-offerings and thanksgiving loaves, and it was [made] of metal, as it is stated in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] Dam Chatat (Zevachim 95b).

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:4:1.hebrew: ביחוד - בינו לביני. רביה דר' ירמיה — רב; רביה דרב — רבינו הקדוש. לישנא אחרינא: בייחוד — בברור, כמו "וידעו ביחוד ששם ארון נגנז" (יומא דף נד.):
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:4:1.english: Beyiḥud - [Meaning] between him and me [i.e., privately]. The teacher of Rabbi Yirmeya [was] Rav; the teacher of Rav [was] Rabbeinu HaKadosh. Another version: beyiḥud [means] clearly, as [in the passage], "and they knew with certainty [beyiḥud] that the Ark was hidden there" (Yoma 54a).

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:4:2.hebrew: פת מרובה - הרבה חררין ביחד. ולאו משום חימוץ נקט לה, ובחררין דקים קאמר, ומשום דקא טרח טירחא דלא צריך הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:4:2.english: A large [quantity of] bread - Many loaves [baked] together. And it is not because of leavening that [the Tanna] stated it; rather, he is speaking of thin loaves, and [it is prohibited] because he is exerting himself with unnecessary labor.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:4:3.hebrew: בלישה - כשלשין אותה, עבה היא העיסה כשהיא כולה ביחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:4:3.english: In kneading - When they knead it, the dough is thick when it is all together.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:6:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: תניא נמי הכי, <abbr title="בית שמאי">ב"ש</abbr> אומרים: אין אופין פת עבה <abbr title="ביום טוב">בי"ט</abbr>, ולא גרסינן בפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:6:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "It was also taught thus: Beit Shammai say: One may not bake thick bread on a Festival," and we do not read "on Passover."

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:6:2.hebrew: תניא נמי הכי - דלאו משום חמץ נקט, אלא משום טירחא, דהא הכא לא תנא פסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:6:2.english: That was also taught - That it was not stated because of leaven, rather because of exertion, for here it did not teach Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:7:1.hebrew: ובסריקין המצויירים - מצות המצויירות. ואע"פ שאמרו לכתחלה אסור, דיעבד שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:7:1.english: And with figured serikin - Figured matzot. And although they said [that] ab initio it is forbidden, after the fact it is fine.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:7:2.hebrew: שוהה עליהן - לציירן, ואין נותנין מהר לתנור, ומחמיצין:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:7:2.english: She tarries over them - To form figures on them, and they do not put [them] quickly into the oven, and they become leavened.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:8:1.hebrew: אפשר יעשה - הצורה בדפוס, ויקבענה בסריק:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:8:1.english: It is possible he will make - the shape with a mold, and set it into the sarik [shaped matza].

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:8:2.english: Immediately - That is to say, quickly, in one push.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:8:3.english: They will say all shaped [matzot] are prohibited, and those of Baitos are permitted - For most bakers do not have that mold.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:9:1.hebrew: לא של כל אדם אמרו - לאסור, דבעל הבית העושה אותן לעצמו אינו חושש לייפותן כל כך, ואינו שוהה עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:9:1.english: They did not say [this] for all people - [meaning] to prohibit [it], for a homeowner who makes them for himself is not concerned to beautify them so much, and does not tarry over them.

Rashi on Pesachim 37a:9:2.hebrew: אלא של נחתומין - העושין למכור, ומקפידין על נויין, ושוהין על ציורן:
Rashi on Pesachim 37a:9:2.english: Rather, [those] of bakers - Who make [them] to sell, and are particular about their beauty, and linger over their shaping.

Tosafot on Pesachim 37a:1:1.hebrew: ובית הלל מתירין - טעמא דבית הלל כדאמרינן (ביצה דף יז.): מערמת אשה ואופה תנור מלא ככרות אע"פ שאין צריכה רק לככר אחד, אבל למלאות התנור פעם אחרת, ליכא מאן דשרי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 37a:1:1.english: And Beit Hillel permit [it] - The reason of Beit Hillel is as we say (Beitzah 17a): A woman may use artifice and bake an oven full of loaves even though she only needs one loaf, but to fill the oven another time, there is no one who permits [it].

Tosafot on Pesachim 37a:6:1.hebrew: תנא בפסח קאי - תימה דלא משני הכי בריש ערבי פסחים (לקמן פסחים צט:), דפריך: "מאי איריא ערבי פסחים" וכו'. וי"ל דהתם פריך משבת דהוי בכל שבוע, ולא שייך לשנויי דנקט ערבי פסחים משום דתנא בפסח קאי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 37a:6:1.english: The tanna is referring to Passover - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] does not answer thus at the beginning of [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (later, Pesachim 99b), where it asks: "Why specifically on the eves of Passover" etc.? And one can answer that there it asks from Shabbat, which occurs every week, so it is not applicable to answer that [the Mishnah] specifically mentioned the eves of Passover because the tanna is referring to Passover.
